(1) Query kafka broker logs and consumer-group state (search terms: 'orders-3', '8841207', 'commit', 'offset', 'fetcher', 'group', 'settlement') over 07:30-09:00Z for any commit/offset record showing whether orders-3's committed offset advances past 8841207 or freezes at it. events.statement: kafka broker logs over 07:30-09:00Z contain ZERO matches for '8841207' and ZERO matches for 'commit': the only orders-3-related broker line is a benign 'log segment rolled for partition orders-3' at 08:15:38Z. There is no broker commit/offset record in either direction, so an explicit committed-offset advance past or freeze at 8841207 could not be observed at the broker.

settlement-service logs contain ZERO lines matching 'offset' across 07:00-10:00Z (total_matched 0), i.e. the consumer never logs a committed-offset value, so no explicit 'committed offset advanced past 8841207' event exists in consumer logs; and no successful-decode line exists (the only 09:00-10:00Z 'deserialize' matches are 91 ERRORs, all 'missing required field qty').

The poison signature is isolated to ONE partition/offset and never spreads: across 07:00-10:00Z settlement-service has 409 ERROR entries in exactly two patterns, ALL naming orders-3@8841207 - 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-<n>@<n>...missing required field qty' (213) and 'poison message: retrying orders-<n>@<n> (attempt <n>), partition blocked' (196). No other partition (orders-0/1/2/4...) or other offset appears in any entry.

The same offset 8841207 is re-read/retried without unbounded progress: ERRORs continue to the LATEST available bucket, with the last entries at 09:58:31Z ('poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt 61790), partition blocked') and 09:58:00Z (attempt 76189), and attempt counters ranging up to 90685. A consumer that had skipped-and-continued past the record would have stopped naming this offset; the retry counter growing to tens of thousands while the offset label never changes is the strongest available substitute for a frozen committed offset.

Lag climb and throughput loss continue unchanged through the latest bucket with no self-healing/recovery dip: settlement-service consumer_lag rose from 53,779.05 (09:40Z) to 61,605.53 (09:59Z) with missing_points 0 and no downward reversal, while request_rate stayed pinned at 0.38-0.44 req/s (mean 0.40) for every minute 09:40-09:59Z vs the ~62 req/s pre-onset level. No recovery dip at any point in the final 20 minutes.

No per-partition lag or committed-offset metric exists on settlement-service (available_metrics are only consumer_lag, cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts), and kafka/settlement logs offer no per-partition commit record either - so the report's strongest substitute for the missing A35/tc-047 telemetry is the CONTINUOUS recurrence of the same orders-3@8841207 error (07:42:14Z to 09:58:31Z, ~136 min) together with the unbroken lag slope.

events.answer: Partial conversion toward near-proof but formally not complete. The broker exposes no per-partition/consumer-group commit records (kafka logs contain zero matches for '8841207' and zero for 'commit' in 07:30-09:00Z), so an explicit commit/offset freeze at 8841207 is NOT directly observed. However, the strongest available substitutes converge: the SAME orders-3@8841207 deserialize ERROR and the 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt N), partition blocked' error recur continuously and unboundedly through the latest bucket (last at 09:58:31Z, attempt counters reaching 76189/90685), with lag still rising monotonically (61,605.53 at 09:59Z) and throughput pinned at ~0.4 req/s below the pre-onset 62 req/s. No successful decode, no higher offset, and no second partition ever appears. This converts the offset-freeze inference from circumstantial to strongly supported (single poison record hard-blocking partition orders-3), but skip-and-continue is not formally excluded because direct per-partition committed-offset telemetry is unavailable.

events.summary: H1 is the only hypothesis consistent with the full body of evidence, and every competing hypothesis has been positively contradicted by data (H2: zero rebalance/poll-timeout entries F15; H3: flat broker ingest + zero under-replicated partitions F16/F22 + two unaffected co-tenants F19/F20/F23; H4: growing lag with healthy producer throughput F17/F21/F22; H5: no downstream error/latency signal, and the errors name the exact partition/offset F12/F38). The core mechanism is VERIFIED: a v2-schema OrderExecuted record at orders-3@8841207 fails v1 deserialization ("missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)") and is retried with "partition blocked", exclusively at that single partition/offset, continuously for ~136 minutes with attempt counters into the tens of thousands while lag climbs monotonically to ~61.6k and throughput pins at ~0.4 req/s with no recovery (F9/F10/F30/F31/F32/F34/F38/F39/F40). This rules out broad schema incompatibility and confirms a single-record block that starves the consumer. The producer side is well constrained: exactly one in-window deployment across all services (order-service v2.16.0 at 07:40Z, whose declared changes are precisely qty->quantity, +venue, v2 header — F1/F25/F26/F27), no other producer on 'orders', and no earlier order-service deploy/config since 2026-04-01. Two residual weaknesses remain (not "blocking" in the sense of being resolvable by obtainable evidence within budget, and neither able to change the ranking): the exact sub-minute ordering of v2-on-the-wire vs the 07:36–07:40Z break is un-pinned (schema-registry timestamp and rollout artifacts do not exist in this dataset — F28, T5), and the hard-block is inferred from repeated same-offset errors + attempt counters + lag slope rather than from committed-offset telemetry (no per-partition offset metric exists — F35/F41, T7). Both are structurally exhausted data sources, not missed queries; T7 explicitly attempted the decisive offsets/commit/per-partition telemetry and it is unavailable. The correct outcome is therefore to accept H1 with confidence capped at 0.80 — high enough to act on (roll back order-service v2.16.0, or add a v2-tolerant reader to settlement-service), but short of 0.9 because the two hops above remain inferred rather than observed. This is the honest ceiling: an outage team should proceed on H1 while treating the producer-timing hop as strongly-but-not-conclusively established.
